questions.question: What is the percentage of the population with access to clean fuels and technology for cooking in the Sustainable Development Report 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**74%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report 2025**, which tracks the global progress toward the **United Nations' 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, indicates that approximately **74%** of the global population has access to **clean fuels and technologies for cooking**.
 
• This indicator is a primary metric for monitoring **SDG 7**, which aims to ensure **access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy** for all people by the **year 2030**.
 
• Access to clean cooking involves the transition from traditional fuels like **wood, charcoal, and coal** to cleaner alternatives such as **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)**, **natural gas**, **electricity**, and **biogas**.
 
• The report highlights that while there has been significant progress in regions like **Central and Southern Asia**, a large "access gap" remains in **Sub-Saharan Africa**, where traditional biomass is still widely used.
 
• Ensuring **74%** access marks a critical step, yet the **2025 report** emphasizes that current trajectories are not yet sufficient to reach the **100% target** set for **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7):**
 
 
• The goal focuses on three main pillars: **universal access to modern energy**, increasing the **renewable energy share** in the global mix, and doubling the global rate of **energy efficiency** improvement.
 
• Energy is central to nearly every major challenge and opportunity the world faces today, including **poverty alleviation**, **food security**, and **climate change mitigation**.
 
 
 
• **Health and Environmental Impacts:**
 
 
• Lack of clean cooking facilities leads to **household air pollution**, which the **World Health Organization (WHO)** identifies as a leading cause of **premature deaths** globally.
 
• Switching to clean fuels reduces **carbon emissions** and prevents **deforestation** caused by the excessive harvesting of firewood.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN):**
 
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report** is produced annually by the **SDSN**, an initiative launched in **2012** under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General**.
 
• It provides the **SDG Index** and **Dashboards**, which assess the performance of all **193 UN Member States** in implementing the **2030 Agenda**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Classifications:** To be considered "clean," technologies must meet specific **emission standards** defined by **WHO guidelines** for indoor air quality.
 
• **Data Sources:** The figures in the **Sustainable Development Report 2025** are aggregated using data from the **International Energy Agency (IEA)**, the **World Bank**, and the **World Health Organization (WHO)**.
 
• **Gender Dimension:** Women and children are disproportionately affected by the lack of clean fuels, as they are typically responsible for **fuel collection** and are most exposed to **indoor smoke**.
 
• **Global Target:** Achieving universal access (**100%**) requires an estimated **annual investment** of billions of dollars, particularly in infrastructure for **electricity grids** and **fuel distribution** in rural areas.
</ul

questions.question: What poverty rate did the State Bank of India project for India in 2024, as reported in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Bank of India (SBI)** Research report, specifically the **Ecowrap** edition, projected that India’s **poverty rate** for the year **2024** would reach **4.6%**.
 
• This projection, discussed in reports updated through **June 2025**, reflects a significant downward trend in the number of people living below the poverty line compared to previous decades.
 
• The report attributes this decline to a robust increase in **per capita income** and a significant shift in rural and urban consumption patterns as recorded in the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES)**.
 
• According to the **SBI** analysis, the reduction in poverty is a result of the government’s targeted **welfare schemes** and the **digitalization** of the economy, which has improved the efficiency of **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT)**.
 
• The **4.6%** figure highlights the success of inclusive growth strategies that have moved a large segment of the **bottom of the pyramid** population into the **lower-middle-class** bracket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI) Ecowrap:** 
 
 
• **Ecowrap** is a flagship economic research publication by **SBI**, led by the Group Chief Economic Adviser, **Dr. Soumya Kanti Ghosh**.
 
• It provides critical analysis on **macroeconomic indicators**, including **GDP growth**, inflation, and social development metrics.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Measurement in India:** 
 
 
• Historically, poverty in India was measured using the **Tendulkar Committee** and **Rangarajan Committee** methodologies based on **Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE)**.
 
• Recent estimates utilize the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23** data to provide a more contemporary view of poverty levels.
 
 
 
• **Government Interventions:** 
 
 
• Schemes like the **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PM-GKAY)**, which provides free foodgrains to over **80 crore** people, have played a pivotal role in maintaining nutritional security and lowering poverty rates.
 
• The **Lakhpati Didi** initiative and **PM SVANidhi** are other examples of schemes aimed at economic empowerment of the marginalized sections.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:** 
 
 
• The **World Bank** defines **extreme poverty** as living on less than **$2.15 per day** (based on 2017 Purchasing Power Parity).
 
• India’s rapid reduction in poverty has been recognized by international organizations like the **UNDP**, noting that the country has successfully lifted millions out of **Multidimensional Poverty**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rural vs. Urban Trends:** The **SBI** report noted that the decline in **rural poverty** has been more pronounced due to increased agricultural productivity and rural infrastructure development.
 
• **Income Inequality:** Along with the reduction in poverty, the report also highlighted a decline in **income inequality** (measured by the **Gini Coefficient**), suggesting that the benefits of economic growth are becoming more evenly distributed across different **decile groups**.
 
• **Data Validity:** The projection for **2024** (reported in **June 2025**) serves as a benchmark for evaluating the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)**, specifically **SDG 1**, which aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere.

2f:T

questions.question: Which of the following Indian states had the honour of hosting the 38th National Games in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **38th edition** of the **National Games** is officially scheduled to be hosted by the state of **Uttarakhand** in the year **2025**.
 
• The **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**, led by its President **P.T. Usha**, confirmed the dates for the event, which will take place from **January 28 to February 14, 2025**.
 
• This marks a significant milestone for **Uttarakhand**, as it will be the first time the state hosts the summer version of the National Games, having previously hosted the **Winter National Games**.
 
• The games will be spread across several cities in the state, including **Dehradun**, **Haldwani**, **Haridwar**, **Rudrapur**, and **Rishikesh**, to utilize existing and newly developed sports infrastructure.
 
• Chief Minister **Pushkar Singh Dhami** has been actively overseeing the preparations, emphasizing that the event will showcase **Uttarakhand's** culture and hospitality while promoting a sports culture in the Himalayan region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goa (37th National Games)**:
 
 
• The **37th National Games** were held in **Goa** in **2023** (October-November).
 
• It featured over **10,000 athletes** competing in **43 different sports** disciplines.
 
• **Maharashtra** topped the medal tally in the **2023** edition, winning the **Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat (36th National Games)**:
 
 
• The **36th National Games** took place in **Gujarat** in **2022** after a gap of seven years.
 
• The event was held across six cities: **Ahmedabad**, **Gandhinagar**, **Surat**, **Vadodara**, **Rajkot**, and **Bhavnagar**.
 
• The **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)** emerged as the overall champion during this edition.
 
 
 
• **History of National Games**:
 
 
• The first-ever **Indian Olympic Games** (later renamed National Games) were held in **1924** in **Lahore** (undivided India).
 
• The **first modern National Games** on the lines of the Olympics were held in **New Delhi** in **1985**.
 
• The primary objective of these games is to identify and nurture athletic talent for international competitions like the **Olympics** and **Asian Games**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: In July 2025, the Union Environment ministry notified which of the following rules aimed at ensuring the remediation of chemically contaminated sites by those responsible for the contamination?

options.text: Environment Protection (Management of Contaminated Sites) Rules, 2025
Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Rules, 2025
Environmental Restoration and Management (Pollution Control) Rules, 2025
Hazardous Waste and Remediation Management Rules, 2025

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environment Protection (Management of Contaminated Sites) Rules, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** notified the **Environment Protection (Management of Contaminated Sites) Rules, 2025** in **July 2025**. These rules represent a significant step in India's environmental governance by focusing on the cleanup of land and water bodies impacted by industrial pollutants.
 
• The core objective of these rules is the **remediation** of sites where **hazardous substances** or chemicals have been released, ensuring that the environment is restored to a safe state.
 
• A fundamental pillar of these rules is the **"polluter pays principle,"** which mandates that the person or organization responsible for the **contamination** must bear the entire **financial liability** for the investigation and remediation process.
 
• A **"contaminated site"** is specifically defined under these rules as a place where the **concentration** of hazardous substances exceeds the **standards** prescribed by the government, thereby posing a significant risk to **human health** and the ecological balance.
 
• The rules empower **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)** and **Pollution Control Committees (PCCs)** to identify such sites, maintain a public **inventory**, and monitor the progress of **remediation plans** submitted by the responsible parties. *Hence, the notification aims at institutionalizing the management of polluted areas.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** These rules are framed under the authority granted by the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, which allows the **Central Government** to take necessary measures to protect and improve the quality of the environment.
 
• **Role of the CPCB:** The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** is tasked with providing the technical **guidelines**, **protocols**, and **remediation standards** that must be followed nationwide to ensure scientific accuracy in the cleanup process.
 
• **Legacy Contaminated Sites:** The rules also address **"legacy sites,"** which are areas contaminated in the past where the original polluter may no longer exist or be identifiable. In such cases, the **State Government** or designated authorities may step in to initiate the **remediation**.
 
• **Stages of Management:** The management process usually involves three critical stages: **Preliminary Investigation** to confirm contamination, **Detailed Site Investigation** to map the extent of the spread, and the formulation and execution of a **Remediation Plan**.
 
• **Impact on Public Health:** Chemically contaminated sites often lead to **groundwater pollution** and **soil degradation**, causing long-term health issues such as **respiratory diseases**, **carcinogenic risks**, and **heavy metal poisoning** among local communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Financial Guarantees:** To prevent the abandonment of contaminated areas, the rules may require industries to provide **financial assurances** or **insurance** to cover potential future remediation costs.
 
• **Public Participation:** The **2025 Rules** emphasize **transparency**, requiring that information regarding **contaminated sites** be available in the public domain so that residents are aware of potential **environmental hazards** in their vicinity.
 
• **Enforcement:** Failure to comply with the **remediation orders** issued by the **SPCB** can lead to heavy **penalties**, **closure of industry**, or legal action under the **Environment (Protection) Act**.
 
• **Sustainable Restoration:** The rules encourage the use of **green remediation** technologies, such as **bioremediation** or **phytoremediation**, which use biological agents to neutralize contaminants in a **cost-effective** and **eco-friendly** manner.

questions.question: In September 2025, the Supreme Court directed the Election Commission of India to treat which of the following documents as the 12th valid proof of identity for inclusion in Bihar’s revised voters’ list?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aadhaar Card**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **September 2025**, the **Supreme Court** issued a significant directive to the **Election Commission of India (ECI)** regarding the electoral process in **Bihar**.
 
• The court ordered that the **Aadhaar Card** be recognized as the **12th valid proof of identity** specifically for inclusion and verification in **Bihar’s revised voters’ list**.
 
• This decision was aimed at addressing discrepancies in the **Electoral Roll** and ensuring a more inclusive registration process for **voters** who may lack other forms of traditional identification.
 
• The **Aadhaar Card**, which is a **12-digit unique identity number** issued by the **Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI)**, serves as a robust tool for verifying the **identity** and **residence** of a person.
 
• The directive emphasizes the use of technology and centralized databases to eliminate **duplicate entries** and **bogus voters** from the revised lists in the state of **Bihar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI):**

 
 
• The **ECI** is an autonomous **constitutional authority** responsible for administering election processes in India as per **Article 324** of the **Constitution**.
 
• It oversees elections to the **Lok Sabha**, **Rajya Sabha**, **State Legislative Assemblies**, and the offices of the **President** and **Vice President**.
 
 
 
• **Valid Identity Proofs for Voting:**
 
 
• Traditionally, the **ECI** accepts several documents for identification at polling stations, including the **Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC)**, **Passport**, **Driving License**, and **Service Identity Cards** issued by **Central/State Government**.
 
• Other recognized documents include **PAN Card**, **MNREGA Job Card**, and **Health Insurance Smart Cards** issued under the scheme of the **Ministry of Labour**.
 
 
 
• **Aadhaar-Voter ID Linking:**
 
 
• The **Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021**, allowed for the voluntary linking of **Aadhaar** with **Voter IDs** to curb the menace of **multiple enrollments** of the same person in different places.
 
• The **Supreme Court’s** intervention often balances the need for **electoral integrity** with the **Right to Privacy** and the **Right to Vote**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bihar State Context:** **Bihar** has **243 Legislative Assembly constituencies** and **40 Lok Sabha seats**, making the accuracy of its **voter database** critical for **National Politics**.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The preparation and revision of **Electoral Rolls** are governed by the **Representation of the People Act, 1950** and the **Registration of Electors Rules, 1960**.
 
• **UIDAI:** The **Unique Identification Authority of India** was established in **2009** and functions under the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**.
 
• **Role of the Judiciary:** The **Supreme Court** acts as a guardian of the **Constitution**, ensuring that the **Election Commission** maintains the **purity of elections** through fair **voter identification** practices.

questions.question: When was the Union Budget 2025–26 presented in Parliament by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 February 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** was presented in the **Parliament** of India on **1 February 2025** by the Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, **Nirmala Sitharaman**.
 
• With this presentation, **Nirmala Sitharaman** created a historical milestone by presenting her **seventh consecutive budget**, surpassing the record previously held by former Prime Minister and Finance Minister **Morarji Desai**.
 
• The budget outlines the **Government of India's** estimated receipts and expenditures for the upcoming **fiscal year**, which runs from **1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026**.
 
• Following the established tradition since **2017**, the budget was presented on the **first day of February** to ensure that the budgetary provisions and tax changes could be implemented by the start of the new financial year.
 
• The presentation was preceded by the **Economic Survey 2024-25**, which was tabled in the house on **31 January 2025**, providing a comprehensive report on the performance of the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provision:** According to **Article 112** of the **Constitution of India**, the President shall, in respect of every financial year, cause to be laid before both the Houses of Parliament a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India, referred to as the **Annual Financial Statement**.
 
• **Budget Date Shift:** Until **2016**, the Union Budget was presented on the last working day of February. In **2017**, then Finance Minister **Arun Jaitley** shifted the date to **1 February** to allow for better administrative planning.
 
• **Railway Budget Merger:** Also in **2017**, based on the recommendations of the **Bibek Debroy Committee**, the 92-year-old practice of presenting a separate **Railway Budget** was discontinued, and it was merged with the Union Budget.
 
• **Digital Transition:** In **2021**, the government introduced the first-ever **paperless budget** due to the COVID-19 pandemic, where the Finance Minister read the speech from a digital tablet, a practice that has continued to promote the **Digital India** mission.
 
• **Bahi-Khata Tradition:** In **2019**, **Nirmala Sitharaman** replaced the traditional colonial-style leather briefcase with a **Bahi-Khata** (a red silk cloth folder) to carry the budget documents, signifying a shift toward Indian traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Halwa Ceremony:** This is a traditional event held at **North Block** in New Delhi, usually a few days before the budget, marking the beginning of the printing (or digital finalization) process and the "lock-in" of finance ministry officials to maintain **strict secrecy**.
 
• **Fiscal Year:** The **financial year** in India follows a cycle from **April to March**, which is different from the calendar year (January to December).
 
• **Vote on Account:** In an election year, the government usually presents an **Interim Budget** or a **Vote on Account** to meet essential expenditures until a new government is formed. Since **2025-26** is not a general election year, a **full budget** was presented.
 
• **Budget Components:** The budget is divided into two main parts: the **Revenue Budget** (short-term income and expenses) and the **Capital Budget** (long-term investments and assets).

__
 
• **Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL)** reached a major milestone by introducing the soft launch of its **homegrown Quantum 5G Fixed-Wireless-Access (FWA)** system.
 
• The event took place on **18 June 2025**, signifying a leap forward for India's public sector unit in the competitive telecommunications landscape.
 
• The launch was conducted in **Hyderabad**, a city recognized as a premier **technology and IT hub** in India, serving as the initial testing ground for this advanced network.
 
• The system is distinguished by being **indigenously developed**, meaning the hardware and software stack were designed and manufactured within **India** under the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
• This **Quantum 5G FWA** system is designed to provide high-speed internet connectivity without the need for physical fiber lines, utilizing **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)** for enhanced security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Quantum 5G Technology**:

 
 
• It incorporates **Quantum Cryptography** to ensure that data transmission is virtually unhackable, addressing modern **cybersecurity** concerns.
 
• By using **quantum mechanics**, the network can detect any eavesdropping attempts immediately, providing a secure platform for **government** and **enterprise** use.
 
 
 
• **Fixed-Wireless-Access (FWA)**:
 
 
• **FWA** allows network operators to provide ultra-high-speed broadband to suburban and rural areas where laying **optical fiber cables** is difficult or expensive.
 
• It utilizes **millimeter-wave (mmWave)** or **mid-band spectrum** to deliver **gigabit speeds** over the air to a fixed receiver at the consumer's premises.
 
 
 
• **Role of BSNL in 5G**:
 
 
• **BSNL** has been working closely with the **Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT)** to deploy an entirely **Indian 5G stack**.
 
• Unlike private players who often rely on foreign vendors like **Nokia** or **Ericsson**, BSNL's focus is on **sovereign technology** to ensure long-term strategic independence.
 
 
 
• **Geographic Impact**:
 
 
• The choice of **Hyderabad** for the soft launch highlights the city's robust infrastructure and the presence of numerous **defense** and **research laboratories** that can benefit from **Quantum-secure** communications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Quantum Mission (NQM)**:

 
 
• The development of this technology aligns with India's **National Quantum Mission**, approved in **2023**, which aims to make India a global leader in **quantum technologies**.
 
• The mission targets **quantum communication** over distances of several hundred kilometers, which **BSNL** is now implementing at a commercial scale.
 
 
 
• **Telecom Sector Evolution**:
 
 
• The transition from **4G** to **Quantum 5G** represents a technological "leapfrogging" for **BSNL**, allowing it to compete with private giants like **Reliance Jio** and **Bharti Airtel**.
 
• As of **2025**, the goal is to expand this service to other major **metropolitan cities** and eventually to **Tier-2** and **Tier-3** towns to bridge the **digital divide**.

questions.question: According to the Sustainable Development Report 2025, what is the percentage of seats held by women in the Indian parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report 2025** indicates that the percentage of seats held by women in the **Indian Parliament** stands at **13.8%**. This metric is a vital indicator for monitoring progress toward **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 5**, which focuses on **Gender Equality**.
 
• In the **2024 General Elections**, which formed the **18th Lok Sabha**, a total of **74 women** were elected out of **543 seats**. This resulted in a percentage of approximately **13.6% to 13.8%**, reflecting a slight stagnation in female political representation.
 
• The current figure of **13.8%** shows a marginal decrease compared to the **17th Lok Sabha** (elected in **2019**), where **78 women** were elected, accounting for **14.36%** of the house.
 
• Under the **SDG Indicator 5.5.1**, the proportion of seats held by women in national parliaments is tracked globally to ensure "women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making."
 
• Despite being one of the world's largest democracies, **India's** percentage remains lower than the **global average** of women in national parliaments, which hovers around **26.5%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Bill):**
 
 
• To address the low representation, the **Government of India** passed the **128th Constitutional Amendment Bill** in **September 2023**.
 
• The Act mandates a **33% reservation** for women in the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• However, the implementation of this reservation is linked to the completion of the next **census** and the subsequent **delimitation exercise**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of Women in Parliament:**
 
 
• In India's **1st Lok Sabha** (formed in **1952**), women held only **4.4%** of the seats.
 
• While the number has grown from **22 women** in **1952** to **74 women** in **2024**, the growth rate has been slow over the last **seven decades**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **SDGs** were adopted by all **United Nations Member States** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty and protect the planet by **2030**.
 
• **SDG 5** specifically targets **gender equality**, including the elimination of all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the public and private spheres.
 
 
 
• **Global and Regional Comparison:**
 
 
• According to reports from the **Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU)**, countries like **Rwanda**, **Cuba**, and **Nicaragua** lead the world with over **50%** women's representation in their national legislatures.
 
• In the **South Asian** region, countries like **Nepal** and **Bangladesh** have historically maintained higher percentages of women in parliament compared to **India** due to various reservation mechanisms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Election Commission of India (ECI):** The **ECI** has noted that while female **voter turnout** has significantly increased (often surpassing male turnout in recent state elections), the number of female **candidates** fielded by political parties remains low.
 
• **Sustainable Development Report:** This report is an annual assessment of progress for all **UN Member States** towards the **SDGs**, published by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**.
 
• **State-wise Performance:** In the **2024 elections**, states like **West Bengal** and **Odisha** showed higher trends of electing women members compared to the national average.

• The championships featured various categories, including the **Men's 10km**, **Women's 10km**, as well as **Under-20**, **Under-18**, and **Under-16** age groups for both boys and girls.
 
• The event served as the official selection trials for the Indian national team to participate in the upcoming **Asian Cross Country Championships**.

• **Cross-Country Running:**

questions.question: How many consecutive Australian Open titles has Jannik Sinner won as of 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jannik Sinner** has won **two consecutive** Australian Open titles as of the conclusion of the **2025** tournament.
 
• He secured his **first** Australian Open title in **2024** by defeating **Daniil Medvedev** in a grueling five-set final, coming back from two sets down.
 
• In **January 2025**, Sinner successfully defended his title at **Melbourne Park**, becoming one of the few players in the modern era to win back-to-back titles at the season's opening **Grand Slam**.
 
• This achievement solidified his position as the **World No. 1** in the **ATP Rankings**, a milestone he first reached in **June 2024**.
 
• By winning in **2024** and **2025**, he has established a period of dominance on **hard courts**, following his victory at the **US Open** in late **2024** as well.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Two.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jannik Sinner:**
 
 
• Born in **San Candido, Italy**, in **2001**, Sinner is the most successful **Italian** male tennis player in history.
 
• He is known for his powerful **baseline game** and exceptional **lateral movement**, which are highly effective on the **hard court** surfaces used in Australia and the United States.
 
• Before his **2024** breakthrough, he led **Italy** to a **Davis Cup** title in late **2023**, defeating **Serbia** and **Australia**.
 
 
 
• **The Australian Open:**
 
 
• The **Australian Open** is the first of the four annual **Grand Slam** tennis tournaments, held annually over the last fortnight of **January**.
 
• It is played at **Melbourne Park** on **Blue GreenSet** hard courts.
 
• Historically, **Novak Djokovic** holds the record for the most men's singles titles at this event, with **10** trophies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Grand Slam Context:** Sinner's **2025** victory marked his **third** total **Major** title, following his wins at the **2024 Australian Open** and the **2024 US Open**.
 
• **Statistical Significance:** Sinner became the first player other than the "Big Three" (Federer, Nadal, Djokovic) to defend an **Australian Open** title since **Andre Agassi** in **2001**.
 
• **Rivalries:** His path to the **2025** title involved high-stakes matches against other top-tier players like **Carlos Alcaraz** and **Novak Djokovic**, signaling a generational shift in men's professional tennis.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following schemes, announced by the Government of India, has a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore to support high-risk, high-impact research and innovation projects across science & technology disciplines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Research, Development & Innovation Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India, during the **Interim Budget 2024-25**, announced a massive corpus of **₹1 lakh crore** to drive **long-term financing** and refinancing for the private sector in the field of research and innovation.
 
• This initiative, often categorized under the **Research, Development & Innovation** framework, aims to provide **50-year interest-free loans** to facilitate large-scale investments in **high-risk, high-impact** projects.
 
• The primary objective of this fund is to encourage **commercialization** of research and foster a culture of innovation across various **Science & Technology** disciplines, supporting the vision of **"Jai Anusandhan"**.
 
• This scheme is designed to help **startups** and **private companies** undertake research that requires substantial capital and has a long gestation period, which traditional banking channels might find too risky.
 
• The allocation is a strategic move to significantly boost India’s **Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD)**, which currently stands at approximately **0.64% to 0.7% of GDP**, by involving private players more aggressively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF):** 
 
 
• The **ANRF Act, 2023** was passed to provide high-level strategic direction for scientific research in the country.
 
• The **ANRF** is set to have a total budget of **₹50,000 crore** over **five years** (2023-28), where a major portion is expected to come from the **private sector**.
 
• It functions as an apex body to seed, grow, and promote **R&D** and foster a culture of research and innovation throughout India’s universities and colleges.
 
 
 
• **Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan, Jai Vigyan, Jai Anusandhan:**
 
 
• The slogan was expanded by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** to include **"Jai Anusandhan"** (Hail Innovation) to emphasize that research is the bedrock of a **Viksit Bharat (Developed India)**.
 
 
 
• **Deep-Tech for Defense:**
 
 
• Alongside the innovation fund, the government also announced a new scheme to strengthen **Deep-Tech technologies** for **defense purposes** and expedite **Atmanirbharta** (self-reliance) in the strategic sector.
 
 
 
• **Department of Science and Technology (DST):**
 
 
• The **DST**, established in **May 1971**, plays a pivotal role in organizing, coordinating, and promoting **Science & Technology** activities in India.
 
• It acts as the nodal agency for identifying and implementing new areas of research that align with the national **Innovation Index** goals.

questions.question: Which organisation released the 'Global Risks Report, 2025', outlining geopolitical, environmental and technological threats?

options.text: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Economic Forum (WEF)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Economic Forum (WEF)** published the **20th edition** of the **Global Risks Report 2025** in **January 2025**.
 
• This annual report is released just before the **WEF Annual Meeting** held in **Davos, Switzerland**, providing a foundation for discussions among global leaders.
 
• The **2025 report** identifies **Misinformation and Disinformation** as the most severe global risk anticipated over the next **two years**, fueled by advancements in **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**.
 
• It outlines a range of threats categorized into **Geopolitical**, **Environmental**, **Technological**, **Societal**, and **Economic** domains.
 
• The report warns of a "**Global Fragmentation**" where the world is moving toward a **multipolar** order, making international cooperation on critical issues like **Climate Change** and **Cybersecurity** more difficult.
 
• According to the findings, **Extreme weather events** and **Critical change to Earth systems** are ranked as the top long-term risks over a **10-year** period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF):**
 
 
• It is an international non-governmental and lobbying organization founded on **24 January 1971** by German engineer and economist **Klaus Schwab**.
 
• The headquarters are located in **Cologny, Switzerland**.
 
• Other major reports published by the **WEF** include the **Global Gender Gap Report**, **Energy Transition Index**, **Global Competitiveness Report**, and **Travel and Tourism Development Index**.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF):**
 
 
• Established in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference**, it is headquartered in **Washington, D.C., USA**.
 
• It primarily releases the **World Economic Outlook** and the **Global Financial Stability Report**.
 
 
 
• **Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD):**
 
 
• An intergovernmental organization with **38 member countries**, founded in **1961** and based in **Paris, France**.
 
• It is well-known for the **PISA (Programme for International Student Assessment)** and various economic and environmental surveys.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP):**
 
 
• The **UNDP** is the **United Nations'** global development network, established in **1965**.
 
• It is most famous for publishing the **Human Development Report (HDR)**, which includes the **Human Development Index (HDI)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Methodology:** The **Global Risks Report** is based on the **Global Risks Perception Survey (GRPS)**, which captures the views of nearly **1,500 experts** from academia, business, government, and the international community.
 
• **Short-term vs. Long-term:** The report distinguishes between immediate crises (**0-2 years**) and structural transformations (**10 years**). While **technological** and **societal** issues dominate the short term, **environmental** risks are the primary concern for the next decade.
 
• **Geopolitical Shifts:** The **2025** report emphasizes the risk of **Armed Conflict** and **Geoeconomic Confrontation**, noting that the breakdown of global norms is leading to a more volatile and insecure world.
 
• **AI and Society:** The report highlights how **synthetic content** (deepfakes) and **AI-generated misinformation** can manipulate public opinion and threaten the legitimacy of **elections** globally.
</ul

questions.question: Where was the 19th India Digital Summit (IDS) 2025 held?
questions.solution:

• **Bharat Mandapam:**
